newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cuts off $40 million in aid to Belarus.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cuts off $40 million in aid to Belarus.

text.p: The United States has cut off $40 million in aid to Belarus due to that country's human rights performance, State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said on Friday.
"We have cut off $40 million in assistance to Belarus," Burns told reporters. "The overall reason is lack of respect for human rights in Belarus."

The U.S. aid had been aimed at helping to dismantle the former Soviet Union's nuclear weapons system within Belarus, Burns said. He noted that all nuclear warheads have already been removed from Belarus.

"Since the warheads are out, we think we can take this action without compromising our own security interest but while sending a very strong message of opposition on their human rights performance," Burns said.
"Yesterday 20 people were rounded up in the streets of Minsk for demonstrating against the government," he said. "There are no political freedoms present right now in Belarus."
Burns said the cut in aid will suspend activities of the Cooperative Threat Reduction Programme, but only after activities for which funds have already been obligated are completed.
One such ongoing programme is the destruction of missile launch pads, Burns said.

Other programmes for which funds were not obligated include the elimination of the infrastructure tied to nuclear weapons, disposal of rocket fuel, radiological surveys and full funding for activity to monitor the export of nuclear and other weaponry, Burns said.

"If human rights certification is possible in 1998 or if the human rights situation improves enough for us to be able to certify it later in 1997, we'd be able to resume funding for these projects," he said.
On Thursday, authorities in Belarus slapped a big fine on a prominent politician and arrested 20 people at a peaceful protest against hardline President Alexander Lukashenko.
